macos.add.backup_info.text: New and changed files are copied to the device. Nothing is ever deleted there: files you delete on this Mac stay on the device, and when a file changes the device keeps its older version too. Nothing done on the device - from a phone, another computer or the web - ever changes or deletes anything in this folder on the Mac. Good for photo archives and backups.
macos.add.backup_info.note: Mac app: the (i) explanation of the kind Back up a folder from this Mac.

macos.add.backup_subtitle.text: One way: this Mac → device (upload only, no deletes)
macos.add.backup_subtitle.note: Mac app: subtitle of the kind Back up a folder from this Mac.

macos.add.backup_title.text: Back up a folder from this Mac
macos.add.backup_title.note: Mac app: one of the kinds of folder offered when adding a folder (a row's title).

macos.add.device_info.text: Pick a folder that is already on the device and a place on this Mac: it is downloaded there and kept the same in both places from then on, changes and deletions included, like the option above. Handy for getting a folder onto a second computer. What is set for it on the device (upload only, kept out of Images) stays as it is.
macos.add.device_info.note: Mac app: the (i) explanation of the kind Sync a folder from the device.

macos.add.local_info.text: The folder is copied to the device, and from then on it is kept the same in both places: files added, changed or deleted on the device (from a phone, another computer or the web) change this folder too, and the other way round. Deleted files go to the Trash on the Mac. The first sync only adds - it never deletes.
macos.add.local_info.note: Mac app: the (i) explanation of the kind Sync a folder from this Mac. "Trash" is the Mac's Trash.

macos.add.local_subtitle.text: Two ways: starts from this Mac
macos.add.local_subtitle.note: Mac app: subtitle of the kind Sync a folder from this Mac: changes go both ways, and the first copy comes from this Mac.

macos.add.local_title.text: Sync a folder from this Mac
macos.add.local_title.note: Mac app: one of the kinds of folder offered when adding a folder (a row's title): a folder on this Mac, kept the same on the device.

macos.add.title.note: Mac app: heading of the panel's first add-folder step, which lists the kinds of folder.

macos.add.what_this_does.note: Mac app: tooltip of the (i) button next to each kind of folder and option when adding a folder.

macos.bluetooth.bad_answer.text: The device sent an answer this app could not read
macos.bluetooth.bad_answer.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: error given to the setup page when the device's answer over Bluetooth couldn't be read.

macos.bluetooth.closed.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: error given to requests still waiting when the Bluetooth setup screen was left.

macos.bluetooth.device_id.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: a row of the list of devices waiting to be set up. {id} is the device's short ID (four letters and digits, such as 04B6), shown on its setup page.

macos.bluetooth.device_older.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: a row of the list of devices waiting to be set up, for a device whose image announces no ID.

macos.bluetooth.enter_password.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: heading above the password field, for a recovered device that keeps the password it had.

macos.bluetooth.language_later.text: The setup page will switch to {language} once the installation starts.
macos.bluetooth.language_later.note: Mac app, setting up a device over Bluetooth: a line under the setup page (the web page the device serves) after the language was changed with the window's language menu while that page was already open. The page changes language only once the device starts installing, so that nothing typed on it is lost; until then it stays in the language it opened in. {language} is the newly chosen language, written by its own name (for example Español, Deutsch); language names are never translated.

macos.bluetooth.looking.text: Looking for a device to set up…
macos.bluetooth.looking.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: heading while it looks for a device announcing its setup over Bluetooth.

macos.bluetooth.looking_detail.text: Power the device on with its disks connected. Until it is set up it announces itself over Bluetooth; keep this Mac near it.
macos.bluetooth.looking_detail.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: under the heading Looking for a device to set up….

macos.bluetooth.not_connected.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: error given to the setup page when a request can't be sent because the Bluetooth link is down.

macos.bluetooth.off.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: heading when this Mac's Bluetooth is off.

macos.bluetooth.off_detail.text: Turn Bluetooth on in Control Centre to find the device.
macos.bluetooth.off_detail.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: under the heading Bluetooth is off. "Control Centre" is the Mac's: use macOS's own name for it in this language.

macos.bluetooth.password_known.text: This Mac signs in with the password you chose in the setup.
macos.bluetooth.password_known.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: small print above the button that syncs this Mac with the new device, when the setup page handed over the password chosen in it.

macos.bluetooth.ready_as.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: once the device is installed; the button to sync this Mac with it follows. {device} is its address (for example cala.off-the.cloud).

macos.bluetooth.ready_home.text: The device is ready on your home network.
macos.bluetooth.ready_home.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: once the device is installed without the Off The Cloud bridge (it is reached on the home network only); the button to sync this Mac with it follows.

macos.bluetooth.ready_maybe.text: If the device has finished installing it no longer answers over Bluetooth - you can use it now.
macos.bluetooth.ready_maybe.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: when the Bluetooth link dropped near the end of the install (a device stops answering over Bluetooth once installed); the button to sync this Mac with it follows.

macos.bluetooth.reconnecting.text: Connection to the device lost - reconnecting. Keep this Mac near it.
macos.bluetooth.reconnecting.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: banner above the setup page while the Bluetooth link to the device is being restored.

macos.bluetooth.sign_in_cancelled.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: error given to the setup page when the person closed the Apple or Google sign-in.

macos.bluetooth.sign_in_failed.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: error given to the setup page when the Apple or Google sign-in couldn't be completed with Off The Cloud.

macos.bluetooth.sign_in_unfinished.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: error given to the setup page when the Apple or Google sign-in came back without a result.

macos.bluetooth.timed_out.text: The device did not answer in time
macos.bluetooth.timed_out.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: error given to the setup page when the device didn't answer a request over Bluetooth within 90 seconds.

macos.bluetooth.unauthorized.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: heading when the app isn't allowed to use Bluetooth.

macos.bluetooth.unauthorized_detail.text: Allow Bluetooth for Off The Cloud in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Bluetooth to set a device up this way.
macos.bluetooth.unauthorized_detail.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: under the heading Bluetooth access is needed. "System Settings > Privacy & Security > Bluetooth" is the path in macOS's settings: use macOS's own names for them in this language.

macos.bluetooth.unknown_provider.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: error given to the setup page when it asks to sign in with a provider other than Apple or Google.

macos.bluetooth.use_device.text: Sync this Mac with my device
macos.bluetooth.use_device.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: button, once the device is installed, that makes this Mac sync with it.

macos.bluetooth.which.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: heading when several devices are waiting to be set up; a list of them follows.

macos.bluetooth.which_detail.text: Several devices are waiting to be set up. Each one's ID is on its setup page, where "Blink its light" shows which box it is. The strongest signal is usually the closest.
macos.bluetooth.which_detail.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device over Bluetooth: under the heading Which device?. "Blink its light" is the setup page's link (use its translation, wiz.*).

macos.connection.cancelled.note: Mac app: a folder's error when a request was dropped because the connection to the device was replaced (for example by a faster route).

macos.connection.closed.note: Mac app: a folder's error when a request was dropped because the app closed the connection (Disconnect, quitting).

macos.connection.no_public_key.text: Unable to fetch the connection's public key
macos.connection.no_public_key.note: Mac app: error when signing in failed because the device didn't send the key the password is encrypted with.

macos.connection.not_connected.note: Mac app: a folder's error, or the device folder picker's, when a request couldn't be sent because the connection to the device was down.

macos.connection.password_rejected.note: Mac app: error for requests that were waiting when the device refused the password.

macos.connection.timed_out.text: The device did not answer in time
macos.connection.timed_out.note: Mac app: a folder's error, or the device folder picker's, when the device didn't answer a request in time.

macos.folders.backup_line.text: Backup · this Mac → device, upload only
macos.folders.backup_line.note: Mac app: the line under a backup folder's name in the panel: one way, from this Mac to the device, nothing deleted there.

macos.folders.cant_read.text: Can't read the folder on this Mac
macos.folders.cant_read.note: Mac app: a two-way folder's error when the folder on this Mac can't be read (no permission, or its disk went away).

macos.folders.checking_count.note: Mac app: a folder's progress while the app compares its files with the device, before the file's name: {done} files checked of {total}. Both are numbers, already formatted.

macos.folders.could_not_list.note: Mac app: a folder's error when the device refused to list the folder without saying why; also shown in the device folder picker.

macos.folders.count.note: Mac app: a folder's progress while it sends or receives files, before the file's name: the file {done} of {total}. Both are numbers, already formatted.

macos.folders.restored_files.text: {files} files had disappeared from the device - restored them from this Mac instead of deleting them here
macos.folders.restored_files.note: Mac app: a two-way folder's note after many of its files vanished from the device at once: the app uploaded them again instead of deleting them on this Mac. {files} is how many (always more than 20), written as plain digits.

macos.images.add_info.text: You can change it later with the eye button on the folder's row. A folder renamed later is a new folder on the device: keep it out of Images again.
macos.images.add_info.note: Mac app: the (i) explanation of the Keep out of Images option when adding a folder.

macos.load.cpu.note: Mac app: label of a row in the pop-up over the storage line: how busy the device's processor is.

macos.load.memory.note: Mac app: label of a row in the pop-up over the storage line: the device's memory in use.

macos.load.storage.note: Mac app: label of a row in the pop-up over the storage line: the device's storage, with a bar and the amount used.

macos.login.message.text: Your folders keep syncing in the background after you restart your Mac. You can change this in Settings.
macos.login.message.note: Mac app: text of the one-time start-at-login question in the panel (and on the setup wizard's last page). "Settings" is the panel's Settings.

macos.login.off_in_system_settings.text: Start at login is switched off in System Settings.
macos.login.off_in_system_settings.note: Mac app: note under Settings' Start at login checkbox when the user said yes but switched the login item off in macOS System Settings (use macOS's own name for System Settings).

macos.login.open_login_items.note: Mac app: link next to that note, opening System Settings at Login Items (use macOS's own name for Login Items).

macos.picker.no_subfolders.note: Mac app: in the device folder picker, when the folder being looked at has no folders in it.

macos.popover.back_up.note: Mac app: the button of the folder chooser that picks a folder to back up. Title Case.

macos.popover.choose_backup.text: Choose a folder to back up to the device. This Mac stays the original.
macos.popover.choose_backup.note: Mac app: message at the top of the folder chooser that picks a folder to back up.

macos.popover.choose_download.text: Choose where to download “{path}” and keep it in sync.
macos.popover.choose_download.note: Mac app: message at the top of the folder chooser that picks where a folder from the device goes on this Mac. {path} is the folder's path on the device (for example /Photos/2024).

macos.popover.quit.note: Mac app: button at the bottom right of the menu bar panel that quits the app.

macos.popover.quit_tip.text: Quit Off The Cloud - folders stop syncing until it is opened again
macos.popover.quit_tip.note: Mac app: tooltip of the Quit Off The Cloud button.

macos.settings.address_placeholder.note: Mac app: placeholder of the address field in Settings once Custom address is ticked. "wss://host/ws" and "host" show the forms an address takes: keep them as they are.

macos.settings.connect_hint.text: Enter your device and its password.
macos.settings.connect_hint.note: Mac app: hint next to the Connect button in Settings, under the device and password fields.

macos.settings.custom_address.note: Mac app: checkbox in Settings that swaps the device name field for a full address field.

macos.settings.custom_address_hint.text: For a device not on the Off The Cloud bridge - your own bridge, Tailscale Funnel, or the local network (ws://192.168.…:8080/ws).
macos.settings.custom_address_hint.note: Mac app: note under the address field once Custom address is ticked. The bridge is Off The Cloud's relay service; Tailscale Funnel is a product name; the address is an example: keep it as it is.

macos.settings.device_name_placeholder.note: Mac app: placeholder of the field in Settings for the device's name on off-the.cloud (shown before ".off-the.cloud").

macos.settings.disconnect_button.note: Mac app: small button in Settings that asks before disconnecting from the device.

macos.settings.disconnect_message.text: All your synced folders are removed from this app, so none of them starts syncing with a different device by mistake. The files themselves stay on this Mac and on the device. You can add the folders again after connecting.
macos.settings.disconnect_message.note: Mac app: text of the inline Disconnect confirmation in Settings. Disconnecting removes every folder from the app; no file is deleted.

macos.settings.retry.note: Mac app: small button in Settings, shown while not connected, that tries to connect again now.

macos.setup.bad_hash.text: The downloaded image does not match its signed checksum, so it was deleted. Try again.
macos.setup.bad_hash.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: error when the downloaded image isn't the signed one (damaged or tampered with): it was deleted.

macos.setup.bad_signature.text: The image's checksum is not signed with the Off The Cloud release key. Nothing was kept.
macos.setup.bad_signature.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: error when the device image's SHA-256 file doesn't carry a valid signature of Off The Cloud's release key: the image can't be trusted, so nothing was downloaded.

macos.setup.card_written.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: write step's main button, once Raspberry Pi Imager has written the card: goes on (and deletes the download).

macos.setup.check_again.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: button that looks again for Raspberry Pi Imager on this Mac, once it is installed.

macos.setup.checking_release.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: under the progress bar before the download starts (the image's signed checksum is fetched first).

macos.setup.come_back.text: When Imager says the card is written, come back here.
macos.setup.come_back.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: small print at the foot of the write step. "Imager" is Raspberry Pi Imager.

macos.setup.done_subtitle.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: under the last step's heading, after this Mac was pointed at the new device. {device} is its address (for example cala.off-the.cloud).

macos.setup.done_text.text: Add folders to back up or keep in sync from the Off The Cloud menu bar icon. The device's own page, in a browser, has your photos, files and settings.
macos.setup.done_text.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: the last step's text: what to do next.

macos.setup.done_title.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: heading of the last step.

macos.setup.download_button.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: first step's main button: starts downloading the device image. Title Case, as the Mac's buttons.

macos.setup.download_progress.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: under the download's progress bar: {done} downloaded of {total}, both sizes already formatted ("120 MB", "560.1 MB").

macos.setup.download_subtitle.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: under the download step's heading: where the image goes (the Mac's Downloads folder).

macos.setup.download_title.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: heading of the download step.

macos.setup.downloaded.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: once the image is downloaded and checked. {file} is the image's file name (off-the-cloud-rpi-lite-arm64.img.xz).

macos.setup.finish_prompt.text: Then finish the setup - WiFi, the device's name, its disks and your password:
macos.setup.finish_prompt.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: above the two ways of finishing the setup (on this Mac, on a phone). Ends with a colon: the choices follow.

macos.setup.get_imager.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: button that opens the Raspberry Pi website, where Raspberry Pi Imager is downloaded.

macos.setup.http_failed.text: The download failed (HTTP {code}). Try again in a moment.
macos.setup.http_failed.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: error when the server refused the image's download. {code} is the HTTP status code, a number (404).

macos.setup.image_deleted.text: The downloaded image was deleted from your Downloads folder.
macos.setup.image_deleted.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: small print once the card is written: the download is gone.

macos.setup.imager_missing.text: Raspberry Pi Imager isn't installed. It's free, from the Raspberry Pi Foundation.
macos.setup.imager_missing.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: write step, when this Mac doesn't have the program Raspberry Pi Imager.

macos.setup.intro_note.text: The download is deleted once the card is written.
macos.setup.intro_note.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: small print under the first step's list.

macos.setup.intro_step1.text: Download the Off The Cloud image (about 550 MB).
macos.setup.intro_step1.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: first step's numbered list, item 1.

macos.setup.intro_step2.text: Write it to the microSD card with Raspberry Pi Imager.
macos.setup.intro_step2.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: first step's numbered list, item 2. Raspberry Pi Imager is a program's name.

macos.setup.intro_step3.text: Put the card in the Pi, connect the disks, power it on and finish the setup here over Bluetooth, or on your phone.
macos.setup.intro_step3.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: first step's numbered list, item 3. "the Pi" is the Raspberry Pi.

macos.setup.intro_subtitle.text: A Raspberry Pi 5 (8 GB) with a microSD card and two USB disks becomes your Off The Cloud device.
macos.setup.intro_subtitle.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: the sentence under the first step's heading: what the device is made of.

macos.setup.intro_title.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: heading of the first step.

macos.setup.on_my_phone.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: title of the choice that finishes the setup in the phone app.

macos.setup.on_my_phone_detail.text: In the Off The Cloud app for iPhone or Android.
macos.setup.on_my_phone_detail.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: under the choice On my phone.

macos.setup.on_this_mac.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: title of the choice that finishes the setup here, over Bluetooth.

macos.setup.on_this_mac_detail.text: Over Bluetooth, with this Mac near the device.
macos.setup.on_this_mac_detail.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: under the choice On this Mac.

macos.setup.open_imager.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: button that opens the program Raspberry Pi Imager with the image.

macos.setup.phone_step.text: In the Off The Cloud app for iPhone or Android, tap Set up a new device. The app finds the device over Bluetooth and shows its setup.
macos.setup.phone_step.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: the phone step's instruction. "Set up a new device" is the phone app's button: use its translation (app.*).

macos.setup.phone_subtitle.text: Keep the phone near the device.
macos.setup.phone_subtitle.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: under the heading Continue on your phone.

macos.setup.phone_then.text: Once it is installed, add the device to this Mac from the menu bar: Settings, then its name and password.
macos.setup.phone_then.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: small print of the phone step: how to sync this Mac with the new device afterwards. "Settings" is the menu bar app's Settings.

macos.setup.phone_title.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: heading of the step for finishing the setup on a phone.

macos.setup.show_in_finder.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: button that shows the downloaded image in a Finder window. Use the Mac's usual wording.

macos.setup.start_subtitle.text: Put the card in the Pi, connect the two USB disks, and power it on. It takes a minute or two to start.
macos.setup.start_subtitle.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: under the heading Start the device. "the Pi" is the Raspberry Pi.

macos.setup.start_title.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: heading of the step after the card is written.

macos.setup.switch_button.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: button of the warning that switches this Mac to the new device, removing its synced folders from the app.

macos.setup.switch_message.text: This Mac is connected to {device}. Switching removes all your synced folders from this app, so none of them starts syncing with the new device by mistake. The files themselves stay on this Mac and on the old device.
macos.setup.switch_message.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: the warning's message before switching this Mac to the new device. {device} is the address of the device it is connected to now (for example cala.off-the.cloud).

macos.setup.switch_title.text: Switch this Mac to the new device?
macos.setup.switch_title.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: title of the warning shown before this Mac starts syncing with the new device while it is connected to another one; answered Switch or Cancel.

macos.setup.verifying.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: under the progress bar while the downloaded image is checked against its signed checksum.

macos.setup.write_step1.text: Insert the microSD card and click {button} below.
macos.setup.write_step1.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: write step's numbered list, item 1. {button} is the button's name, "Open Raspberry Pi Imager".

macos.setup.write_step2.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: write step's numbered list, item 2: what to choose in Raspberry Pi Imager. "Choose Device" is Imager's own button: use Imager's wording in this language.

macos.setup.write_step3.text: Choose OS: scroll down to Use custom and pick {file} in your Downloads folder (it is selected in Finder) - unless Imager already shows it.
macos.setup.write_step3.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: write step's numbered list, item 3: what to choose in Raspberry Pi Imager. "Choose OS" and "Use custom" are Imager's own buttons: use Imager's wording in this language. {file} is the image's file name.

macos.setup.write_step4.text: Choose Storage: your SD card. Everything on it is erased.
macos.setup.write_step4.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: write step's numbered list, item 4: what to choose in Raspberry Pi Imager, and that the card is erased. "Choose Storage" is Imager's own button: use Imager's wording in this language.

macos.setup.write_step5.text: Click Next and answer No to "apply OS customisation settings": the device is set up from this Mac or your phone.
macos.setup.write_step5.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: write step's numbered list, item 5. "Next", "No" and "apply OS customisation settings" are Raspberry Pi Imager's own words: use Imager's wording in this language.

macos.setup.write_subtitle.text: macOS only lets apps outside the App Store write SD cards, so Raspberry Pi Imager does this step.
macos.setup.write_subtitle.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: under the write step's heading: why another program writes the card.

macos.setup.write_title.note: Mac app, Set Up a New Device window: heading of the step that writes the image to the microSD card.

macos.upload_only.add_info.text: Files you delete on this Mac stay on the device and aren't downloaded again; files added or changed on the device still come down. You can turn it off later from the web app or the phone app (the lock on the folder in Files); the files you deleted on this Mac while it was on then come back here.
macos.upload_only.add_info.note: Mac app: the (i) explanation of the Upload only option when adding a two-way folder. "Files" is the app's file browser section.
